title: Coral and the Orbit
premise: Yara Nystrom smuggles memories in sealed coral-glass vials between the warring worlds of Meridian and Halcyon, keeping his head down as the fleet truce ticks toward expiry. When gravity fails for nine seconds system-wide, a dying courier presses a stolen memory into his hands: proof that the war's first strike was falsified by the admiralty itself. Hunted by both governments and the ghost of the courier's daughter, Yara must choose between selling the memory to the highest bidder and broadcasting it free to every world at once. He broadcasts it — ending the war, costing him his ship, his anonymity, and finally giving him a place among the people he once only carried cargo for.
about_author: Bram Okafor is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade aboard container ships before turning to fiction. His work blends the loneliness of long-haul routes with an abiding fascination for what people choose to remember.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Mid-run between Meridian and Halcyon, gravity dies across the whole system for exactly nine seconds; loose cargo floats, a passenger nearly dies, and Yara logs the anomaly no one can explain. Beat: unease beneath routine competence.

chapters.title: Coral Glass
chapters.summary: Flashback-laced chapter establishing Yara's trade: memories decanted into coral-glass vials, each run a moral compromise he refuses to examine. POV Yara. Beat: charming self-deception beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The Courier Who Wouldn't Dock
chapters.summary: A battered courier ship hails Yara, refusing all port clearance, asking him to rendezvous in open space. POV alternating Yara and the courier, Ilsa Vey. Beat: dread dressed as curiosity.

chapters.title: What Ilsa Carried
chapters.summary: Ilsa transfers a single vial and a dead-man's switch keyed to Yara's biometrics, then her ship burns up on reentry under unexplained fire. POV Yara. Beat: guilt arriving before understanding.

chapters.title: Customs at Ceres Gate
chapters.summary: Yara passes through orbital customs carrying the vial inside his own prosthetic hand, lying to an inspector who seems to already know. POV Yara. Beat: claustrophobic tension.

chapters.title: The Daughter on the Dock
chapters.summary: A young woman, Sena Vey, confronts Yara claiming the memory is hers by inheritance — her father died delivering it. POV Sena. Beat: grief weaponized into demand.

chapters.title: Playing the Vial
chapters.summary: Against every rule, Yara samples the memory: a falsified attack order, Meridian's first strike manufactured by its own admiralty. POV Yara inside the memory. Beat: vertigo of truth.

chapters.title: Two Buyers, One Truth
chapters.summary: Both governments' agents make offers — Halcyon wants it as ammunition, Meridian wants it erased. Yara realizes he is now the most valuable man alive. POV Yara. Beat: temptation.

chapters.title: Gravity Flickers Again
chapters.summary: A second nine-second failure hits, localized this time around Yara's ship — someone is using the anomaly as a targeting system. POV Sena. Beat: paranoia.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Code, Revised
chapters.summary: Yara's old mentor, dockmaster Okonkwo, offers sanctuary and hard advice: memories aren't cargo, they're testimony. POV Yara. Beat: reluctant conscience.

chapters.title: Fleet Deadline
chapters.summary: News breaks: the truce expires in eleven days. Both fleets mobilize, and the vial becomes a countdown clock. POV Sena watching mobilization from Halcyon. Beat: ticking dread.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Fuel Depot
chapters.summary: Okonkwo sells Yara's location to Meridian agents to protect his docks; Yara escapes but loses his ship, the Coral Saint. POV Yara. Beat: bitter lesson about belonging bought cheaply.

chapters.title: Stowaway
chapters.summary: Sena stows away on Yara's borrowed hauler; they negotiate an uneasy alliance — she wants justice, he wants out. POV alternating. Beat: friction becoming trust.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath the Ice
chapters.summary: They trace the falsified order to a decommissioned records vault on Europa, seeking corroboration before anyone will believe them. POV Sena. Beat: hope requiring proof.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds, Explained
chapters.summary: In the vault they learn the gravity failures are the admiralty's own hunter-protocol sweeping for the stolen memory — the flickers were never natural. POV Yara. Beat: horror of scale.

chapters.title: Ambush in the Dark
chapters.summary: Meridian agents storm the vault; Sena is captured, Yara escapes with the vial and a choice: trade it for her life or broadcast it. POV Yara. Beat: the theme made flesh — one person versus justice.

chapters.title: The Price of One Life
chapters.summary: Yara arranges the trade, then double-crosses everyone: he delivers a decoy vial, keeps the real memory, and frees Sena mid-exchange in a firefight. POV Sena. Beat: fierce, costly loyalty.

chapters.title: Broadcast Tower Kestrel
chapters.summary: With hours before the truce expires, they seize an ancient deep-space relay capable of reaching every world simultaneously. POV Yara. Beat: desperate resolve.

chapters.title: The Message
chapters.summary: Yara plays the full memory — the falsified strike, the admiralty's confession — raw and unedited, to both fleets massed for war. POV multiple brief voices receiving it. Beat: catharsis through exposure.

chapters.title: Ceasefire, Contested
chapters.summary: Ships stand down in confusion while admiralty loyalists attempt a final strike; rank-and-file crews refuse the order, mutinying peacefully across both fleets. POV Sena. Beat: justice seizing itself outside the law.

chapters.title: What the Courts Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: In the aftermath hearings, Yara refuses reward or pardon, testifying instead so the record belongs to everyone; the admiralty falls, and the worlds begin talking again. POV Yara. Beat: quiet reckoning.

chapters.title: Harbor
chapters.summary: Months later, Yara pilots a small honest ferry between reconciled worlds, Sena beside him; a child asks what he used to carry, and he answers: 'People's better days.' Beat: belonging finally earned, not smuggled.
